summary: CNBC reports on the abrupt September 2023 ouster of Dave Clark, the ex-Amazon executive who had been Flexport CEO for about a year, and the return of founder Ryan Petersen. Petersen publicly blamed Clark for overspending, overhiring and unnecessary leases, but documents and sources cited by CNBC undercut those claims and the 'whistleblower' story. The article also covers the Deliverr acquisition, board dynamics, political friction, a disputed separation offer, and Flexport's clash with Amazon's competing service.
one_line: CNBC details how Flexport founder Ryan Petersen forced out CEO Dave Clark in September 2023, and why evidence for his financial-mismanagement claims looks weak.
key_facts: Flexport founder Ryan Petersen forced out Dave Clark, his hand-picked CEO successor and ex-Amazon executive, on Sept. 5, 2023, about a year into the job, so Petersen could run the company again.
Clark spent 23 years at Amazon and built its logistics network; Flexport was valued at $8 billion by private investors in early 2022.
Flexport bought Deliverr from Shopify for $1.3 billion, announced May 4, 2023; Shopify had acquired Deliverr in May 2022 for $2.1 billion.
Clark negotiated Shopify, already a Flexport investor, into adding $40 million in cash and a framework for a $260 million convertible note to the Deliverr deal.
On Sept. 13 at a Phoenix supply chain conference, Petersen praised Clark for the Deliverr deal while Clark sat in the audience; Clark later said on stage, 'I sort of picked the wrong founder.'
Petersen alleged Clark secretly expanded headcount and took on unnecessary leases; documents and sources close to Clark show Clark worked closely with the board and Petersen on those decisions.

A source close to Petersen claimed a senior finance executive was a 'whistleblower' who said Clark's forecast numbers were 'not real'; Flexport's spokesperson later said there was no whistleblower or financial misconduct.
Clark's lawyers sent Flexport a cease-and-desist letter on Sept. 15 calling the allegations false and defamatory; Petersen has since deleted several posts criticizing Clark.

Flexport's chief legal counsel Chris Ferro told Clark the board had voted to fire him for cause and offered 2 million shares for a separation agreement with nondisclosure and nondisparagement clauses; Clark declined.
Ocean freight prices from Asia to the U.S. West Coast fell 90% by late 2022 from a year earlier, from about $14,500 per container at the start of 2022, hurting Flexport's fee-based business.

Petersen sent Clark a message criticizing a female executive, a registered Republican, for 'far left-wing political activism'; Clark's camp suggests politics may have played a role, which Flexport denies.
On Sept. 12, Flexport launched an end-to-end supply chain service for sellers, led by Parisa Sadrzadeh, the same day Amazon unveiled a similar service at its Accelerate conference.
Flexport ousted CFO Kenny Wagers, lost its HR chief, and had cut 20% of staff in January; more layoffs are expected.
Flexport paid rapper Nelly $150,000 for the launch event, then canceled the performance but still paid him.
